subject: Service availability redress: request for credit calculation and issuance timeline
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@cobaltiq.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cobaltiq.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability incident on 2026-05-11 – request for credit

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the post-incident writeup earlier. We appreciate the detail — our engineering team validated the same windows on our side. Per our contract (Section 4.2 uptime SLA) we'd like to request the formal credit calculation and expected issuance timeline for the outage on 2026-05-11 between 02:40–03:35 UTC affecting inference endpoints in us-west-2.

Concretely we need:
- Eligibility confirmation (was the incident within scope of SLA?)
- Calculation methodology and example numbers (tokens/requests impacted or percentage uptime-based credit)
- Expected approval path and date when the credit will hit our account (we are reconciling invoices)

We are hoping to close this by EOW (May 14). Please let us know if you need any more logs from our side; I attached a short list of the requests we saw.

Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Platform Ops | CobaltIQ
Attachments: cobaltiq-uptime-snippets-20260511-12.csv (log excerpt)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@cobaltiq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service availability incident on 2026-05-11 – request for credit

Alex — thanks for the note and the log snippet. Short answers up-front:
- Eligibility: preliminary yes — the incident crossed our SLA threshold (regional gateway ingress errors leading to sustained 18m outage for capped endpoints).
- Method: we can offer the greater of (a) percentage-of-month uptime credit for the affected region per contract, or (b) a tokens-proportional credit for requests that received 5xxs during the outage. We typically present both methods and let customers choose which to apply; Finance requires a signed approval before issuance.

I attached a draft calculation (service-credit-proposal-20260512.xlsx) with both methods filled in using Redwood telemetry and your provided snippets. High-level numbers:
- Region-level uptime method => 0.6% of monthly invoice (pro rata) => estimated credit $4,200
- Token-proportional method => based on 18 minutes of failed requests => estimated credit $3,750

Marissa — can you review the calc and confirm the preferred method and that we have all required evidence? Ben, flagging for Finance approval routing and whether we should issue as a credit note or invoice adjustment.

Rishi
Director, Account Success | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@cobaltiq.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service availability incident on 2026-05-11 – request for credit

Alex — attaching the detailed worksheet I mentioned (service-credit-proposal-20260512.xlsx). Quick notes:
- We computed both methods across your May billing period. All telemetric sources are listed in tab 'evidence' and reference the CSV you provided.
- Recommendation: issue a credit note (Finance prefers this for bookkeeping) equal to the greater method amount ($4,200) so you receive the maximum remediation available per contract.
- Approval path: Finance (Ben) -> Legal review (standard boilerplate) -> credit issuance via customer portal and email. Target timeline: 5–7 business days after approvals.

If you prefer the tokens method, we can honor that instead — just tell us which you want and I'll route for final sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: service-credit-proposal-20260512.xlsx

Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service availability incident on 2026-05-11 – request for credit

Thanks team — reviewed Marissa's worksheet. Finance approves issuing a credit note for $4,200 (region-uptime method) assuming Legal signs off on the wording. Two quick operational requests:
1) Please consolidate evidence into the PDF redress-approval-note.pdf (include telemetry snippets, timeline, and the spreadsheet summary).
2) For audit trail, we will post the credit as a credit note tied to DEAL-9821 and notify via the customer portal. Can Legal confirm if DocuSign is required for this level (we normally do not require DocuSign for under $10k).

Marissa/Rishi — if you can assemble the single PDF and cc legal@redwood.com I will queue issuance. Alex — expected posting timeframe once approvals cleared: 3 business days.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
